verdicts.flaw_description: Co-intervention confound: 'Each shop moved its machines to a coated carbide insert grade that quarter, and every logged run was cut on one of those machines.' A tooling change that itself shortens cycle time happened in the same quarter and applied to 100 percent of the logged runs, so the 4-7 minute reductions cannot be attributed to the coolant rather than the new inserts.

Uncontrolled confound: 'Throughput at each site fell by half against the earlier quarter.' The supposed control - 'Every stack logged here fired on a fixed duty cycle, the same hours whatever the throughput' - only fixes running hours; it does not sever the direct path from material processed to particulate loading. Half the material through a kiln/dryer/calciner/furnace would lower particulate readings on its own, which is exactly the 8-14 percent direction observed.

The outcome predates the intervention in three of the four sections. 'issued 4 November, measured by 27 September', 'issued 5 June, measured by 28 April', and 'issued 26 August, measured by 3 July' all put the completion measurement weeks BEFORE the lab kit was issued, so those gains cannot have been caused by the kit. Only section Two (issued 8 January, measured 24 March) is correctly ordered.

Selective measurement: 'Figures cover the orders rung up at the new prices, and about a fifth of each line's orders were rung up at the old prices.' Roughly 20 percent of orders are dropped from the numerator period while the 'month earlier' baseline is all orders, and the dropped orders are selected on the very variable under test (which price was charged). Revenue per order across the line could be flat or down even with the reported 4-7 percent on the retained subset.

Per-protocol selection bias: 'Only runs completed end to end on the issued route entered the timing set, and drivers at each depot abandoned the issued route on roughly one run in six.' The ~17 percent of runs excluded are precisely the ones where the new route went wrong (traffic, blockage, driver override) and so are the slowest; timing only the clean survivors manufactures the 5-9 minute improvement.

Compliance-based selection: 'Absence figures cover the pupils on the revised timetable throughout, and about a fifth of each cohort spent weeks on the old timetable.' The excluded fifth are the pupils who did not stay on the new timetable, a group plausibly correlated with poor attendance, and the baseline term covers the whole cohort. The 4-7 percent drop can come from dropping those pupils rather than from the timetable.
